solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Vehicle by the road's struggling to reach source of fuel

parts.note: a car is an everyday vehicle

indicators.note: struggling suggests these words being thrown about and forced into a new order

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter here

explanation.surface: A car and its driver labour along the road trying to reach a petrol station.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'source of fuel' sounds like a petrol pump, but it is the body's food energy; 'struggling' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugars and starches are the nutrients the body burns first for energy, so they are a source of its fuel.

clue.text: Fleece mostly covers golfer somewhere in London

indicators.note: covers means the shortened word wraps around the golfer's name
mostly means the word loses its final letter, keeping most of it

parts.note: to fleece someone is to cheat or swindle them
Ernie Els is a South African golfer, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A golfer is swaddled in a fleece somewhere in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims CHEAT to CHEA, which 'covers' ELS. Chelsea is a well-off district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea is a district of west London, so the vague phrase is a plain example of a place there.

clue.text: Repeatedly thanks plumber, finally turning taps

indicators.note: turning means the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: ta is an informal British thank-you, said here three times over

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word plumber

explanation.surface: A grateful householder keeps thanking the plumber, who is finally turning the taps.
explanation.walkthrough: TA TA TA plus R from 'plumber' gives TATATAR, which 'turning' reverses. The definition 'taps' is the knocking noise, not the plumbing fixtures.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat-a-tat is a series of sharp knocks, the sound of someone tapping on a door.

clue.text: Handyman's bored silly when disc-jockey (old boy) popped in

definitions.note: the clue's 's stands for 'is', so the definition is the handyman himself

indicators.note: popped in means the two short abbreviations are slipped inside the jumbled word
silly suggests the word bored being knocked out of shape into a new order

parts.note: DJ is the standard abbreviation for disc jockey
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A handyman is bored stiff when a radio presenter who went to his old school drops by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bored' reads as weary, but 'silly' makes it anagram fodder, and 'popped in' places the two abbreviations after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd-jobber does assorted small repair and maintenance tasks, which is exactly what a handyman does.

clue.text: River over there encapsulates our country

indicators.note: encapsulates means the first word encloses the second like a capsule

parts.note: yon is an old or dialect word for that thing over there
UK, the United Kingdom, is the home country of this British newspaper's setter

explanation.surface: A river far away somehow contains Britain within it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yukon is a great river of north-west Canada and Alaska, flowing to the Bering Sea.

clue.text: Charge around Asian country commonly after game agreed

indicators.note: after means the country comes after the game in the answer

parts.note: RU is short for rugby union, the game
Nam is the common informal name for Vietnam
OK means agreed

explanation.surface: Fans charge around a far-off country after a match is settled.
explanation.definitionFit: To run amok is to rush about wildly and out of control, charging around.

clue.text: Apprentice misses latest article on state oppression

indicators.note: misses latest means the word drops its last letter

parts.note: a tyro is a beginner or apprentice
an is the indefinite article
NY is the abbreviation for New York state

explanation.surface: A trainee misses the latest report on state oppression.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyranny is cruel and unjust rule, which is oppression by those in power.

clue.text: Composer gets big zero when reviewed around Spain

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters sit around the letter for Spain
reviewed suggests the letters looked over again and set out afresh

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A composer gets a big zero from the critics when a Spanish work is reviewed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when reviewed' signals the anagram, and 'around' puts that jumble round the letter for Spain, the international vehicle code.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Bizet was the nineteenth-century French composer of the opera Carmen.

clue.text: Turned out miserable as first of downpours kicked off

indicators.note: kicked off means that letter is removed from the start of the word

parts.note: dejected means miserable or downcast

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of downpours

explanation.surface: Spectators feel miserable as the first of the downpours arrives just after kick-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kicked off' looks like a match starting; it removes D, the 'first of downpours', from DEJECTED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ejected is to be thrown or turned out of a place.

clue.text: At end of week, daughter stays in owing relatives

indicators.note: At end of picks the final letter of week
stays in means the daughter's letter sits inside the phrase for owing

parts.note: in the red means owing money, in debt

explanation.surface: At the end of the week, a daughter stays at home, owing money to relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred are one's family, the people related by blood.

clue.text: Eileen deigns to travel in noisy part of train?

indicators.note: to travel suggests the letters moving about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Eileen condescends to ride in the noisy carriage of the train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to travel' rearranges EILEEN DEIGNS. The question mark admits the definition is a description rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A diesel engine is the loud locomotive that pulls many trains, a clattering part of the whole.

clue.text: Italians consume such port, travelling round south over the limit?

indicators.note: travelling round means the port's letters go round the pieces for south and over the limit

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, usually just Rio, is a Brazilian port
OTT, over the top, means excessive or over the limit

explanation.surface: Italians drink port and travel round the south, going well over the limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italians consume such' seems to be about the port wine, but it defines the rice dish; 'travelling round' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is a classic Italian rice dish, so it is a food Italians eat.

clue.text: One's in the running store during Christmas briefly

indicators.note: during means the store goes inside the shortened festive word
briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Noel is another word for Christmas
a mine is a store or rich supply, as in a mine of information

explanation.surface: Someone is busy running a shop over the Christmas period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's in the running' looks like a race, but it means a candidate; 'briefly' docks a letter and 'during' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is a candidate put forward for a post or award, someone in the running.

clue.text: Force past performers

parts.note: ex means former or past, as in an ex-partner
an act is a performer or group of performers on a bill

explanation.surface: Former performers are a force to be reckoned with.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact a payment or promise is to force it out of someone, demand and obtain it.

clue.text: Lettering extremely tiny on group of buildings next to gym

indicators.note: on, in an across clue, means the piece for tiny is placed after the group of buildings

parts.note: a block is a group of buildings bounded by streets

indicators.note: extremely picks the two extreme letters, first and last, of tiny

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym

explanation.surface: Very small lettering appears on a block beside the gymnasium.
explanation.definitionFit: Block type is a style of printing in plain, solid capital letters, a kind of lettering.

clue.text: Exactly at that time, seaman carried in sole

indicators.note: carried in means the two pieces are held inside the word for sole

parts.note: sole means single or one
then means at that time
OS is the abbreviation for ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: At just that moment a sailor came in carrying a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' looks like the flatfish but means single; 'carried in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: On the nose is an idiom for precisely or exactly, as with a bet landing just right.

clue.text: Tell wife entering to split sausage

indicators.note: entering means the pieces go into the word for split

parts.note: to burst is to split open
to rat is to tell on someone, to inform

explanation.surface: A wife tells on someone who comes in to split a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: A bratwurst is a German pork sausage, usually fried or grilled.

clue.text: Fruit and eggs knocked back around party

indicators.note: knocked back means the word for eggs is turned to read backwards

parts.note: ova is the Latin plural for eggs
ca, short for circa, means around or approximately
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Fruit and eggs are knocked back around a party.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is botanically a fruit, a large berry with a single stone.

clue.text: Marine animal at side of street moaning like a stray

indicators.note: at side of means the creature sits beside the word for street
moaning is the setter's signal that the word for street is voiced, its sound giving other letters

parts.note: a way is a street or road, as in Watling Way
a fish is a marine animal

explanation.surface: A sea creature on the roadside wails like a lost stray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moaning' is an unusual sound signal: the street word is voiced and spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: A waif is a homeless or neglected child or animal, so being waifish means looking like a stray: thin and forlorn.

clue.text: Audibly signal waiters?

definitions.note: the plural waiters refers to people waiting in line, which the answer names collectively

indicators.note: Audibly means the word for signal is spoken, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: a cue is a signal to act or speak

explanation.walkthrough: 'waiters' looks like restaurant staff, but here it means people waiting in line.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of people waiting their turn is made up of waiters in the literal sense.

clue.text: Parisian who has "one over the eight" needs pain-reliever

parts.note: qui is the French word for who
one more than eight is nine

explanation.surface: A Frenchman who has had one too many needs a painkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one over the eight' is British slang for one drink too many, but here it is plain arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Quinine, from cinchona bark, treats malaria and was long used to bring down fever and ease pain.

clue.text: Introduction of religious rite performed in each country

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the abbreviation for each
Introduction of picks the opening letter of religious
performed suggests the letters of rite being worked into another order

explanation.surface: A religious rite is introduced and performed in every country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Introduction of' takes one letter, 'performed' is the anagram signal, and 'in' places the lot inside the abbreviation for each.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is a country in the Horn of Africa, on the Red Sea coast.

clue.text: Religious adherent gazing centrally is not moving

indicators.note: centrally picks the two middle letters of gazing
moving suggests the letters of is not shifting into a new order

explanation.surface: A devotee stares, motionless, in rapt contemplation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is not moving' suggests stillness, but 'moving' is the anagram signal; 'centrally' takes the middle two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Zionist supports a Jewish homeland in Israel; the clue treats this as a religious allegiance.

clue.text: Stunner did some modelling around mid-Somerset

indicators.note: around means the word is turned to read the other way

parts.note: an artist's model sat for a painter

indicators.note: mid- picks the two middle letters of Somerset

explanation.surface: A beauty did some modelling around the middle of Somerset, a county in south-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stunner' suggests a beautiful model, but it means a stun gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is an electric stun gun, a weapon that stuns its target.

clue.text: Newsman's craft can cut through electronic research

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

indicators.note: cut through means the can goes into the word for research, slicing it

parts.note: a dig is an archaeological research excavation
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A journalist's skill can trim excess from electronic research.
explanation.definitionFit: Editing is the work of preparing and correcting text for publication, a core skill of a newspaper journalist.

clue.text: They crawl over trailer getting into fastenings

indicators.note: getting into means the pieces go inside the word for fastenings

parts.note: ties are fastenings such as cable ties
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
a trailer advertises a film, so it is an ad

explanation.surface: Something slithers over a trailer and gets caught in its fastenings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crawl' means fawning, not creeping along the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Toadies flatter and fawn on the powerful, which is what people who crawl or suck up do.

clue.text: Greek character has men to check amplifier before performing

indicators.note: before means the first pieces come ahead of the word for performing
to check means the men hold or restrain the amplifier inside their letters

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the military term for enlisted men
a mic, short for microphone, amplifies a voice
on means performing, as in on stage

explanation.surface: A Greek has his crew test the sound system before a gig.
explanation.definitionFit: Omicron is the fifteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, a character in that script.

clue.text: Charity worker given test by that woman, disrupting Easter

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British cars
her refers to that woman

indicators.note: disrupting suggests the letters of Easter being broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: A charity volunteer is tested by a woman who disrupts the Easter festivities.
explanation.walkthrough: The test is the MOT, the yearly British roadworthiness check for cars; 'disrupting' is the anagram signal for the holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother Teresa was the Albanian-born nun famous for her charitable work among the poor of Calcutta.
